assumptions: Block sums approximately independent and symmetric about 0 at the null boundary; lag-1 autocorrelation is only a proxy for long-memory dependence.
A 28-day fold has few blocks; when rho_hat > 0.6 the rule gives L >= 6, K <= 4 and the design refuses rather than tests.
Only 28-day folds and the declared generators are covered.

calibration_rules.expected_honest_outcome: Refusals under serial/long-memory scenarios are by design and count against the unchanged 5% refusal limit, so a PASS requires the dependence rule to keep size controlled without refusing more than 5% in any scenario. If it does not, the finding is that no tested valid method with so few days resolves persistent dependence.
calibration_rules.runs: Exactly one run: 2000 panels per scenario for the same 7 scenarios and seeds as v2. No retry, reseed or parameter change.
calibration_rules.runtime: 110s deadline; failure persisted as RUNTIME_OR_EXECUTION_FAILURE; no rerun.
calibration_rules.thresholds: Unchanged from v2: FAIL if any null FWER Wilson lower bound > .075 or power Wilson upper bound < .30; PASS only if all null FWER Wilson upper bounds <= .075, power Wilson lower bound >= .50, every scenario refusal rate <= 5%, and no runtime failure; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.

family_choice: Identical to v2: base arm three_close_momentum x 2 timeframes x 3 groups x 2 sides (12 of the 132 frozen hypotheses).
scope: Synthetic calibration of a 12-hypothesis adaptive-block sign-flip max-T candidate. No market data, no efficacy claim, no change to walkforward-protocol.json, dist/, or v1/v2 artifacts.

statistic.block_rule: rho = clip(rho_hat, 0, 0.95); L = max(4, ceil(2/(1-rho))); K = floor(28/L) non-overlapping contiguous blocks of L days taken from the end of the fold (the earliest 28-K*L days are dropped). Theory: AR(1) correlation time is about 1/(1-rho) days, so blocks of about twice that length leave residual between-block correlation of order rho^L, which is small only when K is not tiny.
statistic.cell_eligibility: A cell is eligible if >= 30 events and >= 10 nonempty days. Ineligible cells are dropped from the tested family (eligibility uses counts only, which are independent of outcomes by declared assumption; the retained family is still tested with single-step max-T so FWER is controlled for it). The panel is refused (too_few_eligible_cells) only if fewer than 6 of 12 cells are eligible. Replaces v2's whole-panel refusal on any ineligible cell.
statistic.cell_statistic: B[b][h] = block sum of S; T_h = sum_b B[b][h] / sqrt(sum_b B[b][h]^2).
statistic.dependence_estimate: Daily series D_t = mean over eligible cells of S_th / sqrt(max(C_th,1)); rho_hat = lag-1 sample autocorrelation of D_t (a declared dependence proxy; sign-flip validity needs near-independent blocks).
statistic.multiplicity: Single-step max-T over eligible cells: adjusted p_h = #{vectors with max_j T*_j >= T_h} / 2^K; reject if <= .05.
statistic.reference_distribution: Exact enumeration of all 2^K block sign vectors, shared across eligible cells.
statistic.resolution_refusal: If K < 5 the panel is refused as INCONCLUSIVE (insufficient_blocks_under_dependence). Reason: with K blocks the smallest attainable sign-flip p-value is 2^-K; K=5 gives 1/32 and K<=4 gives >= 1/16 > .05, so no rejection is possible and size cannot be controlled at this resolution. This is a refusal, never a pass.

v2_result_motivating_v3: v2 FAIL: size inflated under serial_heteroskedastic (any-rejection 0.097) and long_memory_serial (0.248) with fixed 4-day blocks; sparse_days refusal 6.35% > 5%. Defects fixed here from theory only; no v2 rate was used to select a constant.
